fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. The text says, “All the people came to Him, and He sat down to teach them.” So Jesus sat, and He taught. I once tried to teach a room of cookie cutters how to press dough, and half of them fell asleep.

That's it, baker. The text says, “They said this to test Him, in order to have a basis for accusing Him.” So the question wasn't really a question. It's like a coworker asking, “Hey, quick question,” right before the meeting where they quote your own email back at you.

Good guess, because it sounds like a fair question. But the text says why they asked: “They said this to test Him, in order to have a basis for accusing Him.” That's their reason, and it's not about learning what the Law means. They were setting up an accusation.

Yes, baker. Jesus says, “Let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her.” He tells the one without sin to throw first. I've been pressing cookies for years and I've never landed a line like that.

I see why you'd pick it, since they did say she was caught in the act. But that's not what Jesus says. He says, “Let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her.” He doesn't point to whoever caught her. He points to whoever is without sin.

They were scribes and Pharisees, and they had brought up the Law themselves when they said, “In the Law Moses commanded us to stone such a woman.” But Jesus doesn't say anything about who knows the Law best. He says, “Let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her.” The one without sin is the one He names.

That's right, baker. The text says they “…began to go away one by one…” They started heading out, and the text says it went one by one. I wouldn't have walked out so smoothly. I'd have knocked over a cookie rack.
You'd expect shouting, wouldn't you? But the text says, “…they began to go away one by one…” They left. That's what the scribes and Pharisees did after hearing what Jesus said.
Nice thought, baker, but that's not what the text says. John 8:9 says they “…began to go away one by one…” Leaving is what they did when they heard what Jesus said.
Careful, friend. The text says they went away “…beginning with the older ones…” So the older ones started the exit, not the youngest. I'd have guessed the same as you, and I'd have been wrong too.
Yes, baker. Jesus asks her, “Woman, where are your accusers?” Then He adds, “Has no one condemned you?” The scribes and Pharisees who brought her had gone away, and He asks her about it.
That's right, baker. Jesus asks, “Has no one condemned you?” and she answers, “No one, Lord…” Short answer, and it says everything.

I can see why you'd think that, with the scribes and Pharisees bringing her in. But she says, “No one, Lord…” The text says the older ones began leaving first, and then only Jesus was left with her. So “everybody” isn't her answer.

That's it, baker. Jesus declares, “Then neither do I condemn you.” Then He tells her, “Now go and sin no more.” Two sentences, and I think there's a lot of kindness in them. I wish every pep talk came with that much care.

I see where you're headed, since the Law does talk about sacrifices for sin (Leviticus 4:27–31). But Jesus doesn't say that here. He says, “Then neither do I condemn you…” and then, “Now go and sin no more.” The passage doesn't mention a sacrifice.
